transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-12 16:00 PDT / Duration ~62 min / Attendees: Carlos (Redwood CSM), Priya (Redwood SE), Liam (Redwood AE), Nora (Redwood PM), Sofia, Ben, Dana, Marco, Tara

Summary: Quick kickoff focused on sprint-zero objectives for Kodiak Insights' migration to Redwood Dedicated runtime. Covered staging setup, security checklist, baseline perf tests, data flow, and immediate next steps. Some audio glitches caused a couple of words to be garbled; names sometimes mistranscribed.

Topics: 1) Sprint-zero scope and goals 2) Staging VPC & peering 3) Baseline performance tests (latency/throughput) 4) Security / KMS / retention 5) Rollout timeline and success criteria

Action items (brief in-meeting): see metadata action_items list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Carlos: Alright everyone, thanks for joining. This is Carlos from Redwood, CSM for Kodiak, we've got about an hour. I'll quick do an intro then pass to Priya for the runtime handoff.
[00:18] Sofia: Hi hi, thanks. Sofia here. Super excited — hope we can get the staging pieces moving this week.
[00:23] Priya: Great, thanks Sofia. Quick intro — I'm Priya, solutions eng. Today we'll map sprint-zero deliverables and I want to confirm the traffic profile and security items.
[00:34] Ben: Hey all. Ben, platform. We have a VPC in us-west-2 ready but need to understand peering and IAM requirements.
[00:41] Marco: Marco, data eng — I'll own the sample traffic and prompts.
[00:45] Dana: Dana from security — I'll be focusing on KMS and retention.
[00:50] Liam: And Liam here from AE, I'll handle commercial/contract clarity if needed.
[00:54] Carlos: Awesome. Priya, take it away on the runtime orientation.
[01:00] Priya: Cool. So high level, Redwood Dedicated runtime will run in your peered VPC for the pilot. We'll supply a small control plane endpoint for management but inference nodes sit in your VPC; that's the private deployment pattern. Note, there's a small bit of handshaking for the KV cache — sorry, KV cash — key value cache configuration, and we do automated batching.
[01:20] Priya: For sprint-zero we want three things: one, establish staging network and peering; two, run baseline perf — latency and throughput — using our standard 5-prompt suite; three, validate security controls (KMS, audit logs).
[01:34] Marco: Quick q: the prompt suite — is it the same as the one in the onboarding doc or do you want our domain prompts?
[01:39] Priya: Good question. Start with our canonical suite so we can compare against Redwood baselines, then layer your domain prompts. We'll provide a CSV with tokens and expected ranges.
[01:48] Ben: On peering, can you confirm the exact ports/protocols? Our networking team needs those specifics.
[01:52] Priya: Yes — we'll send a peering checklist. Short version: TCP 443 for control plane, gRPC 15001 for internal comms, and some ephemeral high ports for KV sync. I'll put that in the runbook.
[02:06] Dana: For KMS, do you support customer-managed keys (CMK)? We need to ensure keys remain in our tenant.
[02:10] Priya: Absolutely, CMK is supported. It's a config during the initial deployment; Redwood integrates with common KMS providers. We'll surface the exact IAM roles required.
[02:19] Sofia: Anything we should be worried about around token retention or the embedding store? We don't want long-term storage of PII.
[02:26] Priya: Good call. By default we only cache prefixes for performance but you can opt-out of caching for sensitive workloads. Embedding store is optional — if you do use it we'll recommend an encryption-at-rest policy and retention window. We'll add explicit config for PII redaction if you need it.
[02:44] Carlos: Sounds like the security asks are clear. Dana, can you confirm which KMS and what retention windows you expect?
[02:51] Dana: We're using AWS KMS with CMK and require 90-day retention for any non-PII logs and immediate purge for PII. I'll send a checklist.
[02:59] Priya: Noted. For performance, we typically benchmark both cold and warm contexts to capture KV cache benefits. Cold first token latency can be higher; with warm KV you'll see 20–40% improvements depending on prompt length.
[03:16] Marco: Are you using quantizashun options in Dedicated? We need to know possible small model regressions.
[03:21] Priya: Yes we have quantization profiles — 8-bit and mixed. We'll recommend a profile based on your token distribution. We'll also run quality evals on your small prompt set so we can measure any drop.
[03:32] Tara: Quick commercial question — is the pilot meter usage or flat?
[03:36] Liam: For sprint-zero pilot we typically do a timeboxed pilot with usage cap — we'll send a short note. Nothing contract heavy yet.
[03:42] Sofia: Good. On the perf tests, do you need us to simulate concurrency? Our typical peak is ~45 QPS across 3 endpoints.
[03:49] Priya: Yes please. Provide average tokens per request, typical session length, and concurrency. Marco, if you can drop a CSV with per-endpoint QPS, that helps us size the initial nodes.
[03:58] Marco: Will do.
[04:00] [background noise — audio glitch for ~6s, some words missing]
[04:07] Priya: Sorry, can you repeat the last bit?
[04:09] Ben: I asked about observability — what traces and logs are exposed in the console? Need to ensure we can map request IDs to our app logs.
[04:16] Priya: Good — Redwood Console exposes per-request token counts, latency percentiles, model version, and an optional trace ID that you can pass. We'll show the tracing hook in the sprint-zero session. Also exportable CSVs for cost analysis.
[04:29] Carlos: We'll record that as a must-have.
[04:31] Dana: For audit logs, do you retain the audit trail for configuration changes? We need a tamper-evident history.
[04:36] Priya: Yes, config audit logs are retained and can be shipped to your SIEM via our audit-log forwarder. We'll include the retention options in the security snapshot.
[04:48] Sofia: Let's talk timeline: we want a minimal pilot in staging by end of next week — is that feasible?
[04:52] Priya: If we get VPC peering and IAM roles this week, plus your prompt CSV, yes. The main blocker is networking.
[04:59] Ben: I'll prioritize peering today. Expect the peering request by tomorrow EOD.
[05:03] Carlos: Great. We'll aim to schedule the 1.5-hour sprint-zero working session the week of Sep 20. Nora will propose times.
[05:10] Nora: I'll send a calendar invite with an agenda and a list of attendees.
[05:15] Marco: One extra question — fallback behavior: if Dedicated nodes lose capacity, what's the rollback path?
[05:20] Priya: There's an automated routing policy. We can define fallback to a compatible hosted variant with slightly higher latency but still available; it's configurable per-route. We'll demo the failover in the tech deep dive.
[05:33] Sofia: Also want to run a cost sensitivity — can we simulate token cost at different batching configs?
[05:38] Priya: Yes, Redwood Optimize will provide suggested batching and quantization to hit target cost/latency tradeoffs. We'll generate some initial config recommendations after the baseline tests.
[05:48] Dana: Is there a requirement for SSO? We use Okta and need SAML SSO for the control plane.
[05:53] Priya: Okta SAML is supported. We'll include the SSO steps in the onboarding checklist.
[05:59] Sofia: Anything else commercially?
[06:01] Liam: I'll follow up with a short note on pilot licensing and a sample run-rate for the dedicated nodes.
[06:06] Carlos: Alright let's recap: Ben to create peering, Marco to provide traffic CSV, Dana to send KMS/retention checklist, Priya to run perf tests and share runbook, Carlos to send onboarding playbook and security snapshot. We'll reconvene after the first perf run.
[06:22] Sofia: That works. Thanks everyone.
[06:24] Carlos: Thanks, we'll follow up in email.

End of transcript.

References shared: sprint-zero agenda (doc link: https://app.redwood.ai/onboarding/sprint-zero-kodiak), staging runbook (link: https://app.redwood.ai/runbooks/staging-vpc-peering), perf-template.csv (attachment).

Notes on transcription quirks: occasional mis-heard technical words ("KV cash" instead of "KV cache", "quantizashun"), speaker overlap at times, short audio drop ~04:00.
